headline: YORVIPATH growth and a tax windfall swing Ascendis to profit
summary_short: Revenue rose to €246.6M (+144.3% y/y, roughly flat q/q) as YORVIPATH sales nearly quadrupled to €196.9M, while recognition of €679.0M in deferred tax assets helped swing net income to €629.3M from a €94.6M loss a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew 144.3% y/y to €246.6M almost entirely on YORVIPATH's continued global sales growth (€196.9M vs €44.7M), while SKYTROFA fell to €44.0M from €51.3M on a one-time collaboration sale in the year-ago quarter; FX translation cut reported revenue by €22.0M y/y. R&D expenses fell to €59.0M on completed trials and a €10.9M inventory-write-down reversal tied to YUVIWEL's FDA approval, while SG&A rose on commercial expansion; operating profit swung to €24.8M from a €104.2M loss. Net profit of €629.3M was driven mainly by recognition of €679.0M in deferred tax assets, partly offset by €46.8M higher net financial expenses. Cash fell to €572.8M from €616.0M q/q; the company repurchased €51.9M of shares. No formal quarterly or full-year guidance was given.

drivers.explanation: Swing to profit was driven by YORVIPATH's global launch ramp and a large one-time deferred tax asset recognition; SKYTROFA declined against a strong prior-year comparison that included a one-time collaboration sale.

Growth was primarily due to continued growth of YORVIPATH global sales, partly offset by €22.0M of adverse FX translation and a €7.4M SKYTROFA decline versus a one-time collaboration sale a year earlier.
Cost of sales was flat at €17.5M while revenue rose sharply, so nearly all of the revenue increase flowed through to gross profit.
Revenue growth outpaced expenses; R&D fell on completed clinical trials and a €10.9M inventory-write-down reversal from YUVIWEL's approval, while SG&A rose on commercial expansion.
Swing to profit was primarily driven by recognition of €679.0M of deferred tax assets, partly offset by €46.8M higher net financial expenses versus the year-ago period.
Tracks the net income swing to profit; diluted share count rose modestly on warrant exercises and RSU settlements, keeping per-share growth close to net income growth.
Tracks the operating profit swing; depreciation and amortization were roughly flat versus the prior-year and prior-quarter periods.
